hints: Look at the balanced equation first, the mole ratios tell you everything about how much of each substance reacts or forms.
Start with 0.025 mol of sodium carbonate, so you get 0.025 mol of CO2 and need twice as many moles of HCl.
Check each number with n = c x V, gas volume = n x 24000 cm3, and mass = n x Mr, remembering NaCl forms in a 2 to 1 ratio.
walkthrough:
**Find the reacting moles from the equation**

Think of the equation as a recipe. One mole of carbonate needs two moles of acid and makes two moles of salt and one mole of gas.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Check statement 1, volume of CO2**

Mole ratio of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 : \text{CO}_2$ is 1:1, so moles of $\text{CO}_2 = 0.025$ mol. At room temperature and pressure, 1 mol of gas occupies $24000 \text{ cm}^3$.

$$V = n \times 24000 = 0.025 \times 24000 = 600 \text{ cm}^3$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, volume of HCl**

Mole ratio of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 : \text{HCl}$ is 1:2, so moles of HCl needed $= 2 \times 0.025 = 0.050$ mol. Use $n = c \times V$ rearranged.

$$V = \frac{n}{c} = \frac{0.050}{0.2} = 0.25 \text{ dm}^3 = 250 \text{ cm}^3$$
So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, mass of NaCl**

Mole ratio of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 : \text{NaCl}$ is 1:2, so moles of NaCl $= 2 \times 0.025 = 0.050$ mol. $M_r$ of NaCl $= 23.0 + 35.5 = 58.5$.

$$m = n \times M_r = 0.050 \times 58.5 = 2.925 \text{ g}$$
This is double 1.46 g, so statement 3 is incorrect. Statements 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: This would mean statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong because 0.05 mol of NaCl weighs 2.925 g, not 1.46 g.
options.B: This means statements 1 and 2 only are correct. This fits perfectly: 600 cm3 of CO2 is correct and 250 cm3 of 0.2 mol dm-3 HCl is correct, while statement 3 is false.
options.C: This would mean statements 2 and 3 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct, but statement 3 is false and statement 1 is actually correct, so this combination is wrong.
options.D: This would mean statement 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct, so you cannot choose 1 alone.
